answer: Ferrous Path Anchoring. Each agent's messages route only through graph edges witnessed by two-hop neighbors; a new node must attach to existing clusters whose combined path diversity stays below a fixed cutoff. Attacker cost: to reach a meaningful tide of clusters, they must place nodes across many independent regions and pay the latency and bandwidth of maintaining real distinct paths, since clusters that later share an edge get flagged and lose routing weight. A sonnet of repeated joins across overlapping communities collapses, so cheap mass registration fails.
